memory.content: The TUI uses tview.Table/tcell for selectable tabular views, loads AWS data concurrently with region-specific goroutines and channels, and swaps the loading view for the table layout after channel data is collected.

The viewer's recorded IPv4 cost rules are $3.6 per public IPv4 per month as a base, $2.5 for EC2 public IPs, and $2.5 for attached Elastic IPs with a higher charge for unattached EIPs; load balancer public IPs are counted as well.

AWS resources are queried per region: call DescribeRegions once, create each regional client with ec2.NewFromConfig and Options.Region, launch a goroutine per region, aggregate results through channels, and signal completion after the workers finish.
Resource display names prefer the Name tag, then aws:cloudformation:stack-name, then aws:autoscaling:groupName; the getTagValue helper scans []types.Tag and returns the matching tag value.
Table navigation uses SetSelectable(true, false) for row-only selection and SetInputCapture to block Up on the header row and Down on the last row.

The project uses AWS SDK for Go v2 with config.LoadDefaultConfig(context.TODO()), regional clients created with NewFromConfig and an Options.Region override, and no special pagination assumption for the small result sets.

The intended multi-table TUI layout uses tview.NewFlex().SetDirection(tview.FlexRow), AddItem for widgets, and a cost-summary TextView; app.SetRoot(flex, true).SetFocus(firstTable) initializes the layout.
To associate an Elastic IP with a NAT gateway, call DescribeNatGateways and match the EIP allocation ID against NatGatewayAddresses entries, whose PublicIp and AllocationId identify the association.

The current source hardcodes IPv4 cost literals in multiple places; the recorded maintenance direction is to move the $2.5 and $3.6 values into a configurable cost source rather than scattering literals.

skills.name: add-aws-resource-type
skills.description: Extend the Go cost viewer with a new AWS resource, its regional fetcher, table, channel plumbing, and cost calculation.
skills.content: 1. Define the resource information struct and any association fields. 2. Implement fetchXInRegion with an AWS SDK regional client and error handling. 3. Implement fetchAllX across regions using the existing goroutine, WaitGroup, and channel pattern. 4. Add the resource channel to the UI coordination and wait for its result. 5. Create and populate a tview table with stable headers and relevant fields. 6. Add the resource cost to the summary and verify layout ordering. 7. Run gofmt and the relevant Go tests or build.

skills.name: optimize-aws-api-calls
skills.description: Reduce redundant AWS SDK calls by reusing regional work, batching compatible requests, or caching stable metadata.
skills.content: 1. Trace every Describe call from the UI entry point to its regional helper. 2. Identify repeated DescribeRegions, per-item lookups, and sequential calls that can be shared or batched. 3. Preserve region scoping and association correctness while designing a cache or batch request. 4. Add explicit error and stale-data behavior for any cached result. 5. Measure or compare call counts before and after the change. 6. Run gofmt and relevant tests or a build.

skills.name: format-tui-table-columns
skills.description: Change tview table headers, column order, widths, alignment, or display formatting without breaking row population.
skills.content: 1. Locate the table setup, header cells, and row SetCell calls for the target resource. 2. Define the desired headers and their exact column order. 3. Update headers and every corresponding row cell together, including hidden or newly derived fields. 4. Apply widths, alignment, and currency or identifier formatting consistently. 5. Check navigation and summary text after the column change. 6. Run gofmt and compile or test the package.

skills.name: add-tui-keyboard-shortcut
skills.description: Add a safe key binding to the tview/tcell input-capture path for refresh, export, filtering, or navigation.
skills.content: 1. Find the target table's SetInputCapture or shared input handler. 2. Choose a non-conflicting tcell key and document its behavior in the UI help text. 3. Handle the event before default navigation only when the new action owns that key. 4. Trigger the action without blocking the UI or corrupting selected-row state. 5. Preserve header and last-row navigation guards. 6. Run gofmt and manually or programmatically exercise the key path.

skills.name: test-regional-aws-logic
skills.description: Create focused Go tests for regional fetchers and aggregation with mocked AWS SDK responses.
skills.content: 1. Identify fetchXInRegion and fetchAllX behavior, including error paths and aggregation. 2. Introduce narrow interfaces or test seams if the SDK client is currently concrete. 3. Use table-driven cases for one region, multiple regions, empty results, and a regional error. 4. Assert resource fields, region labels, counts, and cost totals. 5. Verify goroutine/channel completion and that one failure does not silently corrupt unrelated results. 6. Run gofmt and go test ./... .

skills.name: audit-go-error-handling
skills.description: Review AWS SDK and TUI failures for fatal process exits, missing checks, and opportunities for graceful degradation.
skills.content: 1. Search all AWS calls and log.Fatalf/log.Fatal sites. 2. Classify startup failures, regional failures, and UI rendering failures by whether the process can continue safely. 3. Replace recoverable fatal exits with returned errors or logged per-region failures while preserving actionable context. 4. Add context deadlines where long-running calls need bounded execution. 5. Ensure channels close and goroutines finish on errors. 6. Run gofmt, tests, and a build, then document any intentionally fatal startup checks.
